result.summary: I recomputed every number in BB8's reading from the five raw dumps with my own scripts, and all of them match. Under v2 at 61b6618a there are 0 occ_wrong, 0 unplaceable, 0 no-op and 0 resolver_mismatch. All 989 of 67889851's v2 failures are grader_elsewhere, split into cohorts of 138, 42, 113, 10 and 686, and every one is occ_agree at the head. The bound span is unchanged and the result replaces exactly that span, checked twice independently on all 989; 100 of those lines (a regex estimate) hold another word with the same spelling, and the edit still landed on the bound one. Of the 2,342 edit_unbound -> refused_unbound cases, 2,292 are on T<n>, 26 on headrime, 12 on head and 12 on endword. The end slot is unchanged in every field on all 7,935 cases. The 191-per-mode residual is all on end (181 other, 7 numeral, 3 hyphen). All 95,220 v1 records are identical to 67889851, and the 705 v1 failures are the same records as fce4bf0f's base failures, so the gate is FAIL on v1 only. v3's literal verdict equals v2's kind on every case at both earlier trees (0 diffs in 91,896 and 190,440), and so do the named, bound and edited texts. Coverage is complete in every dump. The receipt commits and loop.py shas match the worktrees. The receipt's population sha is a content hash that differs from sha256sum only by the trailing newline. In the 40-case seeded sample, all 40 reproduce by hand and when re-derived at wt-61b with slots.resolve and a fresh call to the production swap. Two qualifications. First, the 989 pass only under v3's occurrence contract: v2's literal rule reads them as wrong_word, and the v2 tool cannot replicate the head's lex keyword. Second, the end and endword slots now edit different words on 371 cur line-modes, where at 67889851 they never did: end still edits the unreadable last word, and endword edits an earlier word the grader binds. Smaller notes: the agreement is partly by construction (shared slots.resolve); the 2,342 refusals remove edits of OOV and dialect words; the v3 tool files are untracked and have no dirty-state pin; and the zero counts cover the 3,990-line population only. No worktree or tracked file was modified.

findings.claim: The v3.0 gate never checks where an edit lands when the grader binds nothing. occurrence() returns edit_unbound for ANY edit with bound None, including an edit on a slot that names no word (named None), which v2 failed as wrong_word. edit_unbound feeds only the policy_residual counter, never failures. So the cur-mode '0 failures' cannot catch an edit on the wrong word wherever the grader binds nothing. At 61b6618a no such wrong edit actually exists: the literal column and my independent post-edit check show it. But the v3.0 gate did not establish that. That closes the hole, but under the revised rule 61b6618a's cur scheme reads FAIL (191 per mode), not the 'v1-only FAIL' BB8 reported.
findings.evidence: (a) Three deliberately wrong swaps, fed through the tool's own occurrence() (AST-extracted verbatim from the pinned v3.0), leave the cur-mode failures empty. W7 (unreadable end word, edit the last READABLE word instead): 185 stripped / 186 sung cases, all edit_unbound. W8 (unreadable T<n>, edit the nearest readable neighbour, the 'compacted index' production's docstring forbids): 1,011 / 1,227, all edit_unbound. W3 (T<n> past the line end, edit the last word): 6,669 / 6,235, all edit_unbound. Example: 'O'er the parchment (not a rhyme),' T1 edited to 'O'er zqzq parchment ...' reads edit_unbound. (b) End to end: the pinned v3.0 main() run with quality.loop.swap_at_slot replaced by that broken splice returns failures={v1:stripped:occ_wrong 353, v1:sung:occ_wrong 348}, the same as the genuine 61b receipt. It reports 0 controls failed and 0 negatives failed. Only policy_residual_edit_unbound moves, from 191/191 to 7,855/7,627. In its own dump the literal column reads wrong_word for 7,831/7,604 of those cases. (c) At 61b6618a, all 191 edit_unbound per cur mode have literal agree_unbound, edited == named, with 0 named-None cases. The post-edit check confirms all 191.

findings.claim: The oracle is not independent of production for non-default slots, so '0 occ_wrong' there holds largely by construction. Production's _bound_index and the tool's _bound both read the widx of the same slots.resolve, and both map it through the same reader_line pieces (the tool via reader_token_spans, which is reader_line). The real evidence is narrower: that the splice offsets equal those pieces, plus the refusal counts. I found no path that yields a false occ_agree. The mark is absent from the line, so _edited is an exact single-span reconstruction. The tool's endpoint rule (w[-1]/w[0]), _fold laxness and the missing T<n> index check can only turn a case into a refusal, because production requires a single token and widx == n-1. A casing mismatch would surface as unplaceable_edit, which is a FAIL, not a pass. An independent post-edit check, which needs neither the tool nor raw pieces on the original line, corroborates every occ_agree.
findings.evidence: Post-edit check: splice a readable word, re-read the edited line's token TEXT list, and require the grader's slot on the edited line to bind that word. For head/headrime/endword it also requires that the replaced token was readable. Receipt occ_agree confirmed 33,591/33,591 (stripped) and 39,143/39,143 (sung); edit_unbound confirmed 191/191 each; 0 contradicted. The 22/23 excluded 'transformed' (multi-piece) line-modes, which the tool never tests: production edits them in 222/227 slot cases, and all were confirmed. Synthetic fuzz: 2,470 lines built from repeated mixed-case words, asides holding repeats, numerals, '_110', hyphen and '--' compounds, apostrophes, spaced 's, soft hyphen, NFD accents and '×'. Result: 14,526/15,996 occ_agree, all post-edit ok; 0 occ_wrong, unplaceable, no_op or resolver_mismatch; reader_line pieces ascending in every line.

findings.claim: Q1 (lexicon faithfulness). The tool passes the same build_lexicon('v2','none') object to both swap and oracle. That replicates production only for a run with --lexicon-supplement=v2, no --fallback and no --pronunciations. Production can also pass: --fallback=high|low; supplement none or another version; a lexicon with declared occurrence readings (for_line scoping, Reviser.for_revision); and a freshly built voices lexicon instead of copy.copy. The tool checks keyword NAMES only, not values. loop.py's values come from _lex_cut, which under v1 passes strip_parens=True while _splice passes lex.strip_parens; both are ignored under v1, and the two coincide under v2. My probes: production stays consistent under every variant I could build. Not run: fallback=low.
findings.evidence: Each probe runs the tool's own occurrence() with real production at 61b6618a, cur modes, on the full population. fb_high: bindings moved in 438 (stripped) / 520 (sung) cases, all occ_agree or refused_bound, 0 failures, 0 mismatch. decl (1,508 / 1,817 validated declarations: unreadable first/last tokens made readable, plus a distinct reading on the last occurrence of each repeated word): bindings moved in 1,566 / 1,929 cases, 0 failures, 0 mismatch; examples: 'O'er the parchment' head moves from 'the' to 'O'er', and production follows. supp_none and voices_fresh (SupplementedLexicon(version='v2', strip_parens=False)): identical to the receipt record for record. Supplement v2 (205 rows) changes the readable-token set of 0 of the 3,990 lines, so the receipt says nothing about supplement-dependent bindings. promote: the grader passes promote=self._promote() (revise.py:1645-1648), but resolve forwards promote only to line_anchors for the default slot, whose endpoint is always the last token, so it cannot change occurrence identity.

result.summary:
Every number BB8 cites for 61b6618a reproduces. That includes the 989-case cohort reading occ_agree, the 2,342 refusals (T<n> 2292, headrime 26, head 12, endword 12), 191 edit_unbound per cur mode on end only, 0 cur failures, v1 identical to 67889851 (701 occ_wrong + 4 resolver_mismatch), and an unchanged default end (0 of 15,870 records differ).

An independent post-edit check confirms every occ_agree (33,591 stripped, 39,143 sung) and all 191 unbound end edits per mode; it splices a readable word and asks the grader about the edited line, and needs neither the tool nor raw-piece mapping. A 2,470-line synthetic fuzz found 0 false occ_agree, and code reading shows no path that yields one.

Q1, lexicon: the tool's single build_lexicon('v2','none') object is only one of the lexicons production can pass. I added fallback=high, supplement none, a freshly built voices lexicon, and 1,508 / 1,817 declared occurrence readings. These moved bindings in up to 1,929 cases, with 0 failures. The v2 supplement changes no token's readability in this population, and fallback=low was not run.

Q3, negative controls: they are meaningful. The rig reaches only the oracle (loop._RESOLVE is the real resolve, and production output is unchanged under the rig), and a production that followed the rig would refuse, which reads CANNOT TELL. My own wrong-occurrence swap was caught 1,821/1,821 and 2,213/2,213.

Q2/Q4, the gate (blocking): v3.0 counts every edit where the grader binds nothing as a policy residual and never checks where it landed. That includes phantom-slot edits, which v2 failed. The pinned v3.0 tool, run end to end with a deliberately broken swap, returns the same failures dict as the real receipt, with all controls and negative controls passing. Only the residual moves (191 to 7,855 and 7,627), while its own literal column records 7,831 and 7,604 wrong_word. At 61b6618a no wrong edit is actually hidden: all 191 are literal agree_unbound and confirmed post-edit. But the v3.0 gate did not establish that.

Tool 3.1 appeared mid-review (sha 88237781; I reviewed v3.0, byte-exact, sha c9e282c3). It now fails edit_unbound, which closes this hole. Under 3.1, though, 61b6618a's cur scheme reads FAIL at 191 per mode, so BB8's 'FAIL on v1 only' reading no longer stands.

Further qualifications: the oracle shares slots.resolve and reader_line with production, so cur 0 occ_wrong on non-default slots holds largely by construction. The new end-occurrence check is never exercised by this population. v3.0 drops v2's tree-clean and lexicon pins.
